text.p: Kent Electronics Corp said it agreed to acquire two specialty wire and cable redistribution companies, Futronix Corp of Houston, Texas, and Wire and Cable Specialties Corp of Atlanta, Ga., in a transaction valued at about $65 million.

The agreement calls for the exchange of 2.2 million Kent common shares tock for all of the common stock equivalents of both companies. The transaction also includes assumption of about $20 million in debt that Kent plans to retire upon completion, it said.

In conjunction with the merger agreement, Kent said, its board has terminated the company's share repurchase program. Continuation of the program, an authorization to purchase up to 3 million shares, might preclude Kent from accounting for the merger as a pooling of interests, it explained.
The combined sales of Futronix and Wire and Cable Specialties was over $35 million for the first half of 1996.

Futronix and Wire and Cable Specialties had previously agreed to merge in order to form Futronix Systems Corp, which had planned a 1.9 million share initial public offering at a range of $12 to $14 per share. The IPO would have have represented about 42 percent of the company's stock.
Kent said it has successfully negotiated with Futronix and Wire and Cable Specialties to withdraw this offering and to merge and become a single subsidiary of Kent Electronics.

The company said directors have voted to approve this transaction and increase its authorized common shares to 60 million from 30 million to allow Kent to complete the merger and still have shares available for general corporate purposes.

Both the transaction and the increase in the number of shares must be approved by Kent's shareholders, it said. Completion of the transaction is also subject to approvals by the shareholders of Futronix and Wire and Cable Specialties, and customary regulatory approvals.
